channel.title: Brazil Elections 2026
channel.description: Real-time monitoring of the 2026 Brazilian presidential elections.

item.title: Lula lança nova fase do Desenrola com desconto de até 90% em dívida
item.description: President Lula announced on Monday (4) a new phase of the Desenrola program, offering discounts of up to 90% on Brazilian citizens' debts with financial institutions. The measure, formalized through a provisional measure, takes effect next Tuesday (5) and will last 90 days, aiming to alleviate household indebtedness.

item.title: Bolsonaro recebe alta após cirurgia no ombro
item.description: Former Brazilian President Jair Bolsonaro was discharged from hospital after arthroscopic surgery on his right shoulder and returned to humanitarian house arrest in Brasília. The procedure was authorized by Supreme Court Justice Alexandre de Moraes, and Bolsonaro will wear a sling for six weeks followed by physical therapy. The measure aims at his health recovery, with a new evaluation scheduled after the 90-day house arrest period.

item.title: Senado só olhará para marco legal da cibersegurança após eleições, diz relator
item.description: Senator Jorge Seif (PL-SC), rapporteur of Bill 4752/2025 establishing the cybersecurity legal framework, stated the bill will only advance in the Senate after the 2026 elections, awaiting a change in executive leadership. The proposal, approved by the CCJ and referred to the CCT, is a priority for the GSI and Anatel, whose presidency will become vacant in November. Seif, a co-author of the bill, decided to wait for the election results before presenting his report.

item.title: Zema defende que aposentados não tenham aumento ‘de forma alguma’
item.description: Romeu Zema, presidential pre-candidate from the Novo party, argued that retirees should not receive real increases in their benefits, proposing that payments be tied only to the minimum wage with adjustments solely for inflation. He also suggested increasing the required contribution time for workers as part of a new pension reform.

item.title: Aliados de Lula querem que presidente defenda mandato de ministros no STF
item.description: Lula's allies want him to advocate for term limits for STF ministers, an old idea revived after Jorge Messias's defeat in the Senate confirmation vote and amid the Master case investigations. Messias, Lula's nominee for the STF, views his rejection as a coordinated effort by Davi Alcolumbre, Alexandre de Moraes, and Flávio Dino, though Dino's allies deny involvement. The government is now in a 'war' mode to respond, seeing the episode as a turning point in its relationship with the Court.

item.title: Lula sanciona lei que aumenta penas para furto e roubo
item.description: President Lula signed Law 15.397/2026, increasing penalties for theft, robbery, receiving stolen goods, fraud, and cybercrimes, including raising the penalty for cellphone theft to 4–10 years and for robbery resulting in death to a minimum of 24 years. The law also doubles penalties during public calamities or damage to telecommunications towers. Lula vetoed a proposed increase for qualified robbery (from 7–18 to 16–24 years), arguing it would exceed the penalty for qualified homicide, and the veto will now be reviewed by Congress.

item.title: Bolsonaro tem alta após passar por cirurgia no ombro
item.description: Former President Jair Bolsonaro was discharged from DF Star Hospital in Brasília after surgery on his right shoulder to repair the rotator cuff. He is returning to serve the 90-day house arrest authorized by Supreme Court Minister Alexandre de Moraes. Bolsonaro will wear a sling for six weeks and undergo physiotherapy, amid a long history of surgeries since the 2018 stabbing attack.

item.title: Alckmin lamenta rejeição de Messias ao STF e diz que Corte ficará desfalcada
item.description: Vice President Geraldo Alckmin lamented the Senate's rejection of Jorge Messias for the STF, praising his qualifications and warning that the Court will operate with one fewer justice during a period of high case load. He stated the decision belongs to Congress and downplayed tensions between branches, emphasizing Lula's dialogue-oriented approach. The rejection marked the first time since 1894 that a presidential STF nominee was defeated.

item.title: “Lula está desesperado por medidas populistas”, diz Kataguiri
item.description: Federal deputy Kim Kataguiri (Missão-SP) criticized the second phase of the Desenrola program announced by the Lula government, which allows workers earning up to five minimum wages to use up to 20% of their FGTS balance to pay off debts. In a post on X, he labeled the measure as populist and claimed that Lula is desperate to adopt such actions.

item.title: Lula mira em fim da escala 6x1 por diálogo com evangélicos, e Flávio busca voto católico
item.description: Lula and Flávio Bolsonaro are already shaping religious outreach strategies for the 2026 election: the president aims to ease evangelical resistance through labor policies like ending the 6x1 work scale, while the senator seeks to strengthen his Catholic base, including discussions about nominating Simone Marquetto as vice-president and leveraging ties with figures like Frei Gilson. While Lula leads among Catholics (43% vs 28%), Flávio holds the edge among evangelicals (43% vs 23%), highlighting the religious divide in the electorate.

item.title: Bolsonaro tem alta após cirurgia e deve continuar em tratamento durante 6 a 9 meses, diz médico
item.description: Former President Jair Bolsonaro was discharged from the hospital after undergoing elective arthroscopic surgery on the right rotator cuff in Brasília on Friday, May 1st. The procedure had no complications, and he will wear a sling for six weeks followed by physical therapy, with full recovery expected in six to nine months. The surgery was authorized by Supreme Court Justice Alexandre de Moraes, as Bolsonaro is currently serving a sentence under house arrest for his role in the attempted coup.

item.title: Em busca da popularidade perdida, Lula vira padroeiro dos caloteiros em ano eleitoral
item.description: President Lula announced a new debt relief program, Desenrola 2.0, which will use over R$23 billion from the FGTS, FGO, and dormant bank funds as guarantees to lower interest rates on debt renegotiations, with public money only at risk if debtors default again. The initiative aims to regain popularity among millions of indebted Brazilians dissatisfied with the current government ahead of the 2026 election. Critics argue it uses public funds to shield bad debtors in exchange for electoral support.

item.title: Câmara terá sessão nesta segunda para acelerar prazos do fim da escala 6×1
item.description: The Chamber of Deputies will begin deliberative sessions on Monday to accelerate the analysis of PEC 8/2025, which proposes ending the 6x1 work schedule, aiming to complete the procedural steps by May and vote on the proposal this month. President Hugo Motta intends to align a timeline with the Senate to promulgate the initiative by the end of June, including regional seminars and hearings with Minister Guilherme Boulos.

item.title: Bolsonaro deixa o hospital após passar por cirurgia no ombro e retorna para a prisão domiciliar
item.description: Former Brazilian President Jair Bolsonaro left DF Star Hospital in Brasília after undergoing right shoulder surgery and returned to house arrest at the Solar de Brasília condominium. The arthroscopic rotator cuff repair was authorized by Supreme Court Minister Alexandre de Moraes, as Bolsonaro is serving a 27-year and three-month sentence for crimes including attempted coup d'état and armed criminal organization. Michelle Bolsonaro reported he is recovering well with controlled pain but still requires assistance eating due to his right-arm limitation.

item.title: Zema diz que ministros do STF “se autoaniquilariam” no Japão
item.description: Romeu Zema (Novo), a pre-candidate for presidency, claimed that some Supreme Federal Court ministers would have committed 'self-annihilation' if they served in Japan, criticizing their continued presence due to lack of accountability. He also defended his stance on child labor, stating children should study and bureaucracy hinders hiring young apprentices, and said he is unconcerned about the risk of ineligibility from his public remarks.

item.title: Entidades terão de pagar R$ 600 mil por estimular assédio eleitoral em 2022: ‘Vai virar Venezuela’
item.description: Three business associations from Santa Catarina were ordered to pay R$ 600,000 in collective moral damages for electoral harassment in the run-up to the 2022 presidential election runoff, after organizing meetings with alarmist messages to influence employees' votes in favor of Jair Bolsonaro. The Superior Labor Court (TST) ruled the conduct was abusive, intentional, and illegal, rejecting the freedom of speech defense, as the event aimed to manipulate voting through fear that Brazil would 'become Venezuela'.

item.title: Desenrola 2: Busca pelo termo ‘dívida’ bate recorde no Google e tem alta de 150%
item.description: The launch of the Novo Desenrola Brasil program, Lula's government initiative to renegotiate debts, triggered a 150% increase in Google searches for the term 'debt,' reaching the highest level in the historical series. The program targets families, students, entrepreneurs, and rural farmers, amid a context where over 80 million Brazilians are delinquent, with debts totaling R$ 539 billion in February. Experts warn the impact may be temporary due to high interest rates (Selic at 14.75%) and high income indebtedness, highlighting the contrast between stable macroeconomics and strained household finances.

item.title: Os responsáveis pela articulação para o encontro entre Lula e Trump
item.description: The meeting between Brazilian President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva and Donald Trump, scheduled for Thursday in Washington, was primarily facilitated by Brazilian Foreign Minister Mauro Vieira and U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio. Set to take place one day after Lula’s arrival in the U.S., the discussion will focus on trade, economic policy, and security, with allies viewing it as a positive development for Lula’s agenda following recent congressional setbacks.

item.title: Saiba quais são as 4 categorias contempladas pelo Novo Desenrola
item.description: The New Desenrola 2.0 covers four categories: businesses (micro, small, and women-led), Fies students (with discounts up to 99% for CadÚnico-registered and 77% for non-registered), rural entrepreneurs (with extended Desenrola Rural timeline, reaching 1.3 million people), and families earning up to 5 minimum wages with debts incurred until January 2026 (discounts of 30% to 90%, maximum interest rate of 1.99% per month).

item.title: Aberto credenciamento para a posse do ministro Nunes Marques na Presidência do TSE, em 12 de maio
item.description: The TSE has opened accreditation for the inauguration of Minister Nunes Marques as president of the Court, scheduled for 7 p.m. on May 12 in the plenary in Brasília. Accreditation must be completed by 4 p.m. on the same day, with credentials available for pickup until 5 p.m. During the ceremony, Minister André Mendonça will assume the vice-presidency, and under Marques’ leadership, the TSE will oversee the 2026 General Elections.

item.title: Após pacote do endividamento, Lula mira o fim da taxa das blusinhas
item.description: The Lula government is preparing a provisional measure to eliminate the 20% tax on international purchases under US$50, known as the 'blusinhas tax,' to improve its image amid high rejection and polls showing Flávio Bolsonaro leading in potential 2026 runoff scenarios. The move, backed by the political wing and the Casa Civil, aims to stimulate family consumption, similar to the Novo Desenrola program, though it faces resistance from the productive sector, which warns of job losses and unfair competition with foreign platforms like Shopee, AliExpress, and Shein.

item.title: O novo encontro entre Lula Trump
item.description: President Lula (PT) is set to meet with Donald Trump in Washington on Thursday, March 7, 2026, after the originally scheduled March meeting was postponed due to the outbreak of war between the U.S., Israel, and Iran. The meeting will focus on bilateral cooperation, including combating organized crime, money laundering, arms trafficking, and financial data exchange. The two leaders previously spoke by phone on January 26 for approximately 50 minutes.

item.title: Cinco pontos sobre o Novo Desenrola, pacote de medidas para reduzir o endividamento lançado pelo governo
item.description: The federal government launched the Novo Desenrola Brasil, a debt relief package targeting workers earning up to five minimum wages (R$ 8,105). Key measures include allowing up to 20% of FGTS funds to be used for debt repayment (capped at R$ 8.2 billion), offering 30 to 90% discounts on renegotiated debts, capping interest rates at 1.99% per month, and blocking participants’ CPF in betting houses for 12 months. The program applies to debts incurred before January 31, 2026, that are 90 days to 2 years overdue, including credit cards, overdrafts, and personal loans.

item.title: Tarcísio responde a críticas sobre atuação do PCC em São Paulo: 'Não somos coniventes'
item.description: Governor Tarcísio de Freitas responded to criticisms about the PCC's influence in São Paulo by sharing a video of a Military Police operation in the Paraisópolis favela, stating that the state will not allow criminals to control territories. He accused allies of Fernando Haddad of exploiting crime data to undermine his governance, claiming the PCC grew under governments that denied its existence and that the situation is now different.

item.title: Lula usa R$ 23,2 bi de fundos para beneficiar caloteiros em ano eleitoral
item.description: The Lula government announced the second phase of the Desenrola Brasil program, allocating up to R$ 23.2 billion from the FGTS, FGO, and forgotten bank funds to provide 30% to 90% discounts on credit card, overdraft, and personal loan debts. The initiative, which benefits defaulters, is financed by workers and taxpayers, and could affect the Union’s primary balance if the proposed R$ 5 billion FGO top-up is approved.

item.title: Lula: Desenrola Brasil ajudará população a "tirar corda do pescoço"
item.description: President Lula announced the new Desenrola Brasil program, aimed at helping individuals earning up to five minimum wages renegotiate credit card, overdraft, and personal loan debts to 'take the rope off their neck' and regain access to credit. He emphasized that debt should be incurred responsibly and in line with income, criticizing the exclusion of citizens from the formal financial system over small debts. The initiative includes a guarantor fund and bans online betting for one year for participants in the debt renegotiation process.

item.title: Desenrola 2.0: programa prevê desconto de dezenas de bilhões de reais para devedores do Fies
item.description: The Lula government announced Desenrola 2.0, a debt renegotiation program for the Fies student loan fund, offering discounts of 77% to 99% for students with debts overdue for more than one year, benefiting over one million borrowers. The measure, enacted via provisional measure, would provide discounts exceeding R$ 46 billion on a total overdue debt of R$ 61 billion, as the government considers these credits difficult to recover.

item.title: Oposição aposta que STF não abraçará causa de aliados de Lula contra dosimetria
item.description: Opposition lawmakers believe the Supreme Court will not support Lula’s allies who sought to judicially block Congress’s override of the president’s veto on the Dosimetry Bill, arguing that legislative authority belongs to Congress. They note that the Court itself previously acknowledged Parliament’s competence on the matter and that justices were consulted during the bill’s drafting. Despite this, some Lula allies filed a case at the STF but remain skeptical of its success, fearing a ruling in favor of the Judiciary could worsen the ongoing conflict between the Legislative and Judicial branches.

item.title: O presidencialismo de coalizão morreu, eis o autoritarismo parlamentar
item.description: The article argues that Brazil's coalition presidentialism has ended, replaced by a 'parliamentary authoritarianism' where Congress holds unlimited power without checks and balances. This shift weakens the Executive and Judiciary, turning even elected presidents into hostages of Congress, regardless of popular mandate. The author contends this new regime has profound implications for Brazilian democracy and economic policy.

item.title: O que Lula e Trump vão tratar durante encontro na Casa Branca
item.description: Brazilian President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) will travel to the United States for a bilateral meeting with Donald Trump on Thursday (May 7) at the White House. Key topics on the agenda include the U.S. effort to designate Brazilian criminal factions (PCC and CV) as terrorist organizations — a move Brazil opposes — , U.S. tariffs on Brazilian goods, and the ongoing war in the Middle East, which Lula has strongly criticized.

item.title: Justiça nega pedido para apagar vídeo de Nikolas com deboche contra Lula e Janja
item.description: The Federal District Court denied a request to remove a video posted by federal deputy Nikolas Ferreira (PL-MG) that mocked First Lady Janja da Silva while showing President Lula hugging a supporter. The woman featured in the video sought the video’s removal and compensation, but the judge ruled the content, though derogatory, is protected under freedom of speech. The case remains ongoing, with a conciliation hearing scheduled for May 25, 2026.

item.title: Avanço de investigação sobre Lulinha vira novo risco eleitoral para Lula, diz cientista político
item.description: The advancing investigation into Fábio Luís Lula da Silva, known as Lulinha, poses a new electoral risk for President Lula, according to political scientist Rafael Cortez. The case, already underway by the Federal Police, could be exploited by the opposition as a rhetorical weapon, particularly if new revelations emerge from plea bargains, increasing the government's political vulnerability amid already high disapproval ratings.

item.title: Lula e Trump devem conversar na Casa Branca sobre tarifas, minerais críticos, facções criminosas e guerra no Irã
item.description: Brazilian President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva will travel to the United States to meet with President Donald Trump at the White House on Thursday. The meeting will address tariffs on Brazilian exports, the U.S. war against Iran, the activities of criminal factions in Latin America, and the exploration of critical minerals.

item.title: Lula se reunirá com Trump na Casa Branca na quinta; o que se sabe
item.description: President Lula is set to meet with Donald Trump at the White House on Thursday, May 4, following a period of tension between Brazil and the U.S. over the arrest and release of former deputy Alexandre Ramagem in the United States. The meeting signals an effort to improve relations after informal interactions at the UN General Assembly in September 2025 and official phone calls, despite prior U.S. retaliatory measures such as a 50% tariff on Brazilian imports and the inclusion of Supreme Court Justice Alexandre de Moraes in the Magnitsky Act.

item.title: Lula lança plano para renegociação de dívidas; saiba como funcionará o Novo Desenrola
item.description: The Lula government launched the New Desenrola Brasil program to renegotiate debts for families, students, companies, and rural farmers, backed by the FGO with a maximum interest rate of 1.99% per month. Desenrola Famílias offers discounts of 30% to 90%, allows repayment over up to four years, and includes a 12-month CPF block for betting houses. The program also permits partial use of FGTS to settle debts and sets a cap of R$15,000 per person and financial institution.

item.title: Áudio: Diminuição da jornada de trabalho está em pauta no Congresso
item.description: Congress is debating proposals to reduce the weekly workweek from 44 to 40 hours. Bill PL 1.838/2026, from the Lula government, aims to end the 6x1 work schedule and has been given urgency for voting. Meanwhile, PEC 148/2015, proposed by Senator Paulo Paim (PT-RS), calls for a gradual reduction over four years and is ready for plenary vote.

item.title: Desenrola 2.0 para empresas terá condições melhores para negócios liderados por mulheres; entenda
item.description: President Lula launched Desenrola 2.0, featuring Desenrola Empresas, which improves credit conditions for micro and small businesses using public FGO guarantees. Women-led enterprises will receive higher credit limits, accessing up to 60% of annual revenue (capped at R$180,000), compared to 50% for others. Key changes include up to 24 months of grace period, 96-month repayment terms, and 90-day tolerance for late payments before new credit eligibility.

item.title: Cientista político explica por que ‘fator Trump’ pode influenciar disputa Lula x Flávio
item.description: Political scientist Rafael Cortez argues that the prolonged Middle East conflict, intensified by Donald Trump's policies, is increasing inflationary pressure in Brazil, particularly through rising oil prices, which directly affect the cost of living and voter sentiment. Despite the negative economic impacts, Cortez suggests that growing rejection of Trump could politically benefit Lula, as the Brazilian opposition is symbolically linked to the international conservatism associated with the former U.S. president.

item.title: Lula viajará aos EUA nos próximos dias para encontrar Trump, diz fonte
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva will travel to the United States in the coming days to meet with President Donald Trump, according to a Brazilian government source. The meeting is expected to strengthen bilateral relations between the two nations.

item.title: Lula lança novo Desenrola mirando reeleiçăo, com perdăo a dívidas de até R$ 100
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva launched on Monday (4) the new version of Desenrola, a debt renegotiation program that includes forgiveness for debts up to R$100. The measure aims to alleviate indebtedness among low-income workers and is seen as part of Lula’s re-election strategy for 2026. The program seeks to strengthen popular support among vulnerable voters ahead of the upcoming elections.

item.title: Alexandre de Moraes busca aliados de Lula para dizer que năo trabalhou contra Messias
item.description: Supreme Court Minister Alexandre de Moraes sought out Lula's allies to state that he did not work against Jorge Messias' nomination as Attorney General of the Union to the Senate, which ultimately rejected the name. The move aims to clarify his position amid speculation about alleged political influence in the decision.

item.title: Eleitores cativos
item.description: Although last week was difficult for Lula, his candidacy should not be ruled out, as the presidential outcome depends on voters, not Parliament. Despite unfavorable signals from the legislature, popular support remains a decisive factor in determining the next president.

item.title: Por que o próximo presidente da República pode mudar o perfil do STF
item.description: The next Brazilian president will have the power to appoint up to three Supreme Court justices, potentially reshaping the Court’s ideological balance. This influence has grown after Congress rejected Jorge Messias’s nomination, increasing pressure to fill the vacancy left by Luiz Roberto Barroso’s early retirement. Depending on whether Lula or Flávio Bolsonaro wins, appointments will reflect personal loyalty and ideology — Lula favoring trusted allies, while Bolsonarism leans toward conservative figures aligned with its base.

item.title: Ministros se incomodam com STF citado em campanhas, mas divergem sobre reação; leia bastidor
item.description: STF ministers express concern over the electoral use of criticism against the court by pre-candidates, but disagree on the response: while the group aligned with President Edson Fachin favors discretion and occasional official notes, the politically active wing led by Flávio Dino and Gilmar Mendes pushes for a firmer stance, including articles and social media attacks. Despite the backlash, polls show that controversies have not prevented declining approval for candidates like Romeu Zema, whose support dropped from 64% in December 2024 to 52% in August 2025.

item.title: Cinco partidos exibem propaganda partidária nesta semana em rádio e TV
item.description: This week, five political parties are airing partisan advertisements on radio and television between 7:30 PM and 10:30 PM on April 5, 7, and 9, 2025. The PSB leads with six minutes of airtime, followed by PT and Podemos with three minutes each, PP with two minutes, and União Brasil with 30 seconds. The broadcasts occur in the first semester of 2026, as permitted by electoral law during election years.

item.title: ONG vai pedir ao TSE reativação de partido negro extinto no Estado Novo
item.description: The Nova Frente Negra Brasileira NGO will file an action with the TSE to reactivate the Partido da Frente Negra Brasileira, which was extinguished during the Estado Novo in 1937. The organization argues the party was never officially deactivated by the Judiciary or by its own decision, and that its 1936 registration could not be annulled by an executive decree. The reactivation seeks to recognize the party as Brazil’s first and only Black party, with a legacy of fighting racism and promoting education and professional inclusion.

item.title: Dívidas dos brasileiros terão desconto médio de 65% no Novo Desenrola, diz Durigan
item.description: The Novo Desenrola Brasil program, launched by the federal government, offers an average 65% discount on citizens' debts, with interest rates reduced from 15% to 1.99% per month and installment plans of up to four years. The measure was signed by President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva to address rising household debt, which currently stands at 49.9% of annualized income.

item.title: Crânio de dinossauro com mais de 100 milhões de anos voltará ao Brasil
item.description: The skull of the dinosaur Irritator challengeri, illegally excavated in Brazil and taken to Germany in 1991, will be returned to Brazil following an agreement between Presidents Lula and Chancellor Merz. The fossil, the most complete of its family worldwide, had been fraudulently altered with plaster and automotive putty to inflate its black-market value. The repatriation was driven by a campaign led by paleontologist Aline Ghilardi, inspired by the successful return of Ubirajara jubatus in 2023.

item.title: Presidente do DC diz ter barrado Witzel por já haver 'doidos demais' na sigla; ex-governador nega ter feito investida
item.description: Democracia Cristã (DC) president João Caldas said he blocked former Rio governor Wilson Witzel's party affiliation, claiming the party already has 'too many crazies'. Witzel denied this, stating he was approached by Aldo Rebelo and remains affiliated with the Democrat Party since 2022, maintaining his pre-candidacy for Rio de Janeiro governor.

item.title: Sancionado aumento de penas para furto, roubo e receptação
item.description: President Lula signed Law 15.397/2026, which increases penalties for theft, robbery, receiving stolen goods, and virtual crimes such as online scams and cellphone theft. Originating from Bill 3.780/2023 by Deputy Kim Kataguiri, the law raises imprisonment for theft from one to four years to one to six years, with aggravating factors for nighttime offenses, essential infrastructure theft, and specific items like cellphones, firearms, and domestic animals. The general penalty for robbery is also increased from four to ten years to six to ten years.
